T000002725290.title: [Elis SA, 2022 Sales/ Trading Statement Call, Jan 30, 2023](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$DOCID_T000002725290)

text: Would you be willing to give us the numbers, how much pricing has contributed to the organic growth in Q2? [#527](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003194583-527)
And in particular, if you could comment on how price increase contributing to the organic revenue growth in Q4. [#189](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002725290-189)
So it's a good year of price increase. [#539](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003194583-539)
So 10 years ago, we had a profile where we delivered more or less between 2.5% and 3% organic growth on a regular basis. [#551](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003394029-551)
So all in, organic growth was 5.2%. [#191](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003394029-191)
You're raising your organic growth guidance. [#378](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003194583-378)
Let me first reiterate the comment I made on organic growth in October. [#118](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002725290-118)

If you compare what is the organic growth rate of Elis now and where we were 3, 4, 5 years ago, we say now that we'll deliver on a regular and constant basis, at least 4% of organic growth, even with an environment of very low level of inflation. [#358](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003194583-358)
Let's look at the breakdown of full year and Q4 organic revenue growth by geography. [#29](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002725290-29)

Organic growth was driven by the performance of Sweden and the Baltics, where the outsourcing trend continues, but Denmark was tougher with some exceptional losses due to our pricing discipline. [#102](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003194583-102)
Q4 revenue increased plus 20.7% of which 15.7% organic. [#16](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002725290-16)
Pricing was also a significant top line growth driver in the context of a significant minimum wage increase in the region. [#151](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003394029-151)
So in your presentation, you show a waterfall chart with the main factors contributing to organic revenue growth in 2022. [#187](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002725290-187)
Pricing was also a significant top line growth driver in the context of significantly wage increase in the region. [#110](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003194583-110)

And finally, the increasing share of our revenue that is generated in countries with strong organic revenue growth, such as in Latin America or in Eastern Europe will mechanically contribute to the improvement of the group total organic growth. [#393](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002760050-393)

Pricing also contributed to 2024 revenue growth with our pricing policy aiming to offset the inflation of our cost base, which was mainly driven by the increase in salaries. [#36](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003394029-36)
Starting with organic growth that we expect slightly below 4%, factoring in a circa 0.3% negative calendar impact. [#383](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003394029-383)

As Xavier explained earlier, the spectacular organic growth of 21% was pushed by a stronger pricing impact contributing for 8% and the recovery in hospitality for [indiscernible], the rest coming from the regular trend of commercial dynamism, development of resourcing, CSA-linked contract wins and churn improvement. [#178](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000002760050-178)

The 5.2% organic revenue growth was driven by the success of the commercial initiatives we put in place across the board, along with the strengthening of our sales force. [#34](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003394029-34)
The mix of the growth is very good. [#454](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003194583-454)
